solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Eccentric journalist who vacated houses

indicators.note: houses means holds inside, so the emptied word wraps around the journalist
a vacated word has been emptied, so only the outside letters of who remain

parts.note: a hack is a jobbing journalist

explanation.surface: A newspaper reporter with odd habits who has moved out of several homes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' looks like dwellings but is the containment signal, and 'vacated' means only the outer letters of the word who are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Whacko is informal for crazy or wildly odd, a synonym for eccentric.

clue.text: Poor start for rebel dons summoned to court

indicators.note: to don is to put on, so the phrase wears the letter inside it

parts.note: to be had up is British informal for being brought before a court

indicators.note: the start for a word is its opening letter, here of rebel

explanation.surface: Rebellious university fellows are hauled before the court, which is a bad beginning for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dons' looks like academics but means puts on: HAD UP takes R inside. Being 'had up' is British slang for being charged in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard up is an idiom for short of money, so it means poor.

clue.text: Charles worked with them to provide protection for crown

indicators.note: worked suggests the letters are kneaded or reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: Prince Charles collaborated with some people to guard the royal crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked' rearranges CHARLES plus THEM.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorcyclist's helmet protects the top of the head, which is the crown in the anatomical sense.

clue.text: Unknown number supporting past attraction exaggerated

indicators.note: in a down answer a supporting piece sits beneath the others, so it comes last

parts.note: over means finished, in the past
a draw is something that attracts crowds
n stands for an unspecified number in algebra

explanation.surface: Some mystery figure is propping up a former crowd-puller that was overhyped.
explanation.definitionFit: An overdrawn portrayal is overstated, laid on too thick, as an exaggerated one is.

clue.text: Most acute threat to crops on allotment reduced

indicators.note: in an across answer one piece on another follows it, so the pest comes after
reduced means cut short, so the last letter of the synonym goes

parts.note: an allotment is a share or portion
a pest is an insect or animal that damages crops

explanation.surface: The worst menace to the vegetables on a garden allotment has been cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' drops the last letter and 'on' puts the pest after it. An allotment is a British rented vegetable plot, but here it means a portion.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharpest is the superlative of sharp, a synonym of acute, as in keenest.

clue.text: Lascivious youth's debut in racist novel

indicators.note: in places the single letter inside the rearranged letters
novel means new, so the word racist is given a new arrangement
a debut is a first appearance, so take the opening letter of youth's

explanation.surface: A young person's first appearance in a bigoted book is lewd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges RACIST to SATRIC, and 'in' puts Y, from 'debut', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Satyric relates to satyrs, the lustful woodland creatures of myth, so it means lecherous.

clue.text: Range partly divided by motorway

indicators.note: divided by means split open with something put in the gap

parts.note: partly means to some extent, a bit
M is the British abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: A mountain range is partly split by a major road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divided by' puts M inside A BIT.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambit is the scope or extent of something, its range.

clue.text: Sweep pile up

indicators.note: in a down answer up means the word is written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: nap is the raised pile on cloth or carpet

explanation.surface: Brush the heap into a mound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns NAP around.
explanation.definitionFit: To pan a camera is to swing it across a scene, sweeping over it.

clue.text: Equine, unlikely one to have child astride

indicators.note: astride means with legs either side, so the child's letters go round the others

parts.note: a son is a child
tall as in a tall story, one hard to believe
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A horse, though it seems improbable that one would carry a child on its back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astride' has the child's letters straddle the others. Equine is used here as a noun, a horse, and 'unlikely' recalls a tall story.
explanation.definitionFit: A stallion is an uncastrated male horse, an example of an equine animal.

clue.text: Military force, male, the last word in cunning

indicators.note: in puts the first pieces inside the word for cunning

parts.note: art means craft or guile
amen is the word said at the end of a prayer

explanation.surface: An army that is all men and the ultimate in craftiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the last word' is the word ending a prayer, and 'in' places it with the male letter inside the synonym for cunning.
explanation.definitionFit: Armament means weaponry or the armed strength of a nation, its military force.

clue.text: Christian writer sees no point returning

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: nay is an old word for no
the nub is the central point of a matter

explanation.surface: A devout author finds no purpose in going back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses both pieces together. Christian is the hero of The Pilgrim's Progress, so the writer is that book's author, not just a believer.
explanation.definitionFit: John Bunyan wrote The Pilgrim's Progress, whose central character is named Christian.

clue.text: Game abandoned, being pressed for time

parts.note: RU is rugby union
shed means cast off or discarded

explanation.surface: The match was called off because there was no time left.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling rushed means hurried, short of time to do things.

clue.text: Old bag's name withdrawn, breaking law

indicators.note: breaking means splitting open, with another piece in the gap

parts.note: a rule is a law

indicators.note: withdrawn suggests drawn back, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: to cite is to name, as in a lawsuit

explanation.surface: An elderly woman's name was taken off a list for breaking the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawn' reverses the verb for naming before 'breaking' puts it in the law. Old bag reads as an insult to a woman but is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A reticule was a small drawstring handbag carried by women in earlier centuries.

clue.text: After pet disturbed chefs, anger flares

indicators.note: after shows the jumbled cooks come after the pet

parts.note: a cat is a common pet

indicators.note: disturbed means upset or thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: ire is anger

explanation.surface: Once the cat has upset the cooks, tempers flare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' scrambles the cooks, and 'After' sets them behind the pet, with anger at the end; 'flares' is the definition, not anger flaring.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that catches fire bursts into flame, so it flares up.

clue.text: Captain Nemo manoeuvring to secure island's freedom

indicators.note: to secure means to hold fast, so the rearranged letters enclose the island
manoeuvring means moving around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Jules Verne's submarine captain steers his craft to capture an island and win independence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvring' scrambles the captain's name, and 'to secure' wraps it round the island letter. Nemo is the captain of the Nautilus in Verne's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Emancipation is the act of setting people free from bondage or restriction.

clue.text: Smallest chum takes a shot at fattest's bottom

parts.note: a pal is a chum
taking a shot at something means trying it

indicators.note: in a down answer the bottom of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: The tiniest friend has a go at the rear of the heaviest person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottom' takes T from fattest's.
explanation.definitionFit: Paltriest is the superlative of paltry, meaning trivially small or meagre.

clue.text: Surveyor's bill slashed by two pounds

indicators.note: slashed by means cut open with something put in the cut

parts.note: a bill is a poster stuck on a wall
L is the abbreviation for pound sterling, so two pounds give two Ls

explanation.surface: A surveyor's invoice has been cut by a couple of pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slashed by' cuts the bill open for the pounds. Surveyor means someone who runs opinion surveys, not a land surveyor.
explanation.definitionFit: A pollster conducts opinion polls, surveying the public.

clue.text: Republic's green capital

parts.note: a common is a village green
capital means accumulated money, wealth

explanation.surface: A country's environmentally friendly city.
explanation.walkthrough: A common is open public land, as a village green is. Commonwealth was also the name of England's republic under Cromwell.
explanation.definitionFit: A commonwealth is a state governed for the common good, a republic.

clue.text: Mean church in Ely disheartened diocese

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the remaining letters of Ely
a word losing its heart loses its middle letter

parts.note: par is the average or mean level

explanation.surface: A miserly church in the cathedral city of Ely leaves the diocese dispirited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' removes the middle of Ely and 'in' sets the other pieces there. Mean is the average, not stingy; Ely is a small English cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: An eparchy is a diocese of an Eastern Church, the territory under a bishop.

clue.text: Fit men one hopes to unionise?

parts.note: to suit is to fit or be right for
OR is other ranks, enlisted soldiers rather than officers

explanation.surface: Fit workers who hope to form a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: Unionise is read as uniting in marriage, not organising labour; the question mark flags the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitor is a man courting a woman and hoping to marry her.

clue.text: Naval detachment crossing loch, all of it dispersing

indicators.note: crossing means spanning, so the jumbled letters go across the loch's letter
dispersing means scattering, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for loch, a Scottish lake

explanation.surface: A fleet sailing across a Scottish lake is breaking up and scattering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispersing' rearranges ALL OF IT to FOTILLA, and 'crossing' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A flotilla is a small fleet of ships, often a unit split off from a navy.

clue.text: Assurance given with no initial projection

indicators.note: with no initial means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a pledge is a promise or assurance

explanation.surface: A promise given without a first forecast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no initial' drops the P from PLEDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A ledge is a narrow shelf jutting out from a wall or cliff, a projection.

clue.text: Improper question used primarily during mutiny

indicators.note: during means within the time of, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: a rise or rising is a revolt

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of question is used

explanation.surface: An unsuitable question was mainly asked in the middle of a revolt aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' puts Q inside RISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Risqué means slightly indecent or near the knuckle, so improper.

clue.text: Accumulated rent covered by son and daughter

indicators.note: covered by means enclosed, so the family letters go round the middle piece

parts.note: rent here is the past tense of rend, tore

explanation.surface: The rent money built up was paid by a boy and a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered by' puts TORE between S and D. Rent is the verb rend, not a payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Stored means kept or laid up for later, collected over time.

clue.text: Scrap that fiery opponents may well lose

definitions.meaning: a scrap of cloth, a remnant

definitions.text: that fiery opponents may well lose
definitions.meaning: to lose one's ... is a British idiom for losing one's temper

explanation.walkthrough: Scrap looks like a fight, in keeping with the fiery opponents, but it is a bit of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A rag is a scrap of old cloth, and losing it is slang for flying into a temper.

clue.text: Bigot, heading to the back after commander gets on

indicators.note: after shows the moved word follows the commander

parts.note: CO is commanding officer

indicators.note: the heading, the opening letter, moves to the end of the word

parts.note: a sexist is a bigot about gender

explanation.surface: A prejudiced officer is posted to the rear after the commanding officer boards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading to the back' moves the S of SEXIST to the end, making EXISTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Coexists means lives alongside others in harmony, as someone who gets on with them does.

clue.text: Smugness rife at first in Tamworth farm?

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the farm word

parts.note: a Tamworth is a British breed of pig, so its farm is a pig farm

indicators.note: at first means the opening letter of rife is used

explanation.surface: Self-satisfaction is rampant from the start on a pig farm in a Midlands town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts R inside PIGGERY. Tamworth is also an English town, but here it is the ginger pig breed.
explanation.definitionFit: Priggery is the behaviour of a prig, a self-righteous and complacent person.

clue.text: Proposal from right-wing to co-opt ambassador

indicators.note: to co-opt is to take in a new member, so the word for right-wing takes in the other piece

parts.note: a Tory is a right-wing Conservative
HE is His Excellency, an ambassador's title

explanation.surface: A conservative plan to bring a diplomat on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to co-opt' has the party word take in the ambassador. An ambassador is addressed as His Excellency, abbreviated in crosswords to two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is a proposition put forward to explain something, a proposal.
